svg.title: claudia composes — how text flows around a floating object (decided 2026-11-17)
svg.desc: Four wrap modes on the same paragraph: over the text, around the object, above and below, behind the text; the one key that cycles the modes and the grab cursor for an object behind the text; the rules that make screen and print agree; the mapping to DOCX and ODF; and the open points.
svg.text: claudia composes — text flowing around a floating object

Decided on 2026-11-17 (D1061–D1064); the wrap itself is not built yet. Until now an object floats over the words and nothing wraps (D179). Content is invented. The engine lays the lines out first: see the architecture sheet.
A · Four ways, on the same paragraph

A new object starts as Above and below; a document with no wrap saved stays Over the text, so no existing one changes. The wrap belongs to the object's place in the text, not to the picture: the same picture can be over the words in one text and around in another.
1 · Over the text
no wrap saved, as today
· Lines run full width underneath.
· The object is opaque and hides what it covers.
· Nothing moves when the object does.
2 · Around the object
the lines make room
· Lines shorten to the object's box plus a distance.
· A side narrower than 3 em stays empty.
· Text resumes in full width below it.
3 · Above and below
the default for a new object
· Lines stop above the box and go on under it.
· The object stands alone on its lines.
· Good for a figure with a caption.
4 · Behind the text
a watermark, a stamp
· Drawn under the words, which stay readable.
· Lines run full width over it.
· Reached with Ctrl held (grab cursor, B) or by Tab.
distance
B · One key: Format ▸ Wrap Text, Ctrl+Alt+L
Each press moves the held object to the next mode and is one step in the history.
The menu entry shows the current mode and a screen reader announces it.
Format ▸ Wrap Text: Around
Ctrl+Alt+L
Over
Around
Above/below
Behind
…and back to Over
Ctrl
held
Over a Behind object's area
the cursor is a hand; a click
takes the object, not the text.
Tab and Edit ▸ Select Next Object reach it without a pointer. Distance: where it is set is open.
C · The rules, so that screen and print agree
Each line asks one question: how wide am I here? The answer comes from the objects that reach its band.
box + distance = the band; a line takes
the widest free stretch(es) of its own band
The object's place comes first, from the layout
without this object's wrap: the character's line, plus
dx and dy. So an object never moves the line it hangs
from, and no loop is possible.
Objects are taken in the order of the text. An object
only changes lines at and after its top; the lines
above it stay as they were.
A line's available width is its column minus every
band that reaches it. A stretch narrower than 3 em is
not used, so no single word is stranded beside an
object.
An object keeps to its page: if it will not fit above
the bottom margin it is moved up (D907), and its wrap
applies on that page only.
The same arithmetic runs in the layout library for the
page view and print, and in a test that compares the
lines the editor shows (stage 2, D1062).
D · What Word and LibreOffice call them
Import and export, so that wrap survives the round trip.
Claudia
DOCX (wp:anchor)
ODF (style:wrap)
over the text
wrapNone
run-through, foreground
around
wrapSquare + dist*
parallel + fo:margin
above and below
wrapTopAndBottom
none
behind the text
wrapNone, behindDoc
run-through, background
Not modelled: tight and through (a contour round the picture),
in line with the text. They come in as the nearest of the four,
and the original is kept untouched and written back on export,
so a document passing through Claudia does not lose it.
ODF values are from memory of what LibreOffice writes: check
against a file it wrote before any import code (as with rotation).
Decided on 2026-11-17, and what is still open
1 Who lays the lines out (D1062)
Decided: the engine first, for print and the print preview. The editor keeps the
browser's lines until a second stage puts a float of the object's size at the
anchor's line; a test compares which lines the float and the engine narrow.
Details on the architecture sheet.
2 Selecting a Behind object (D1063)
Decided: Ctrl held while the pointer is over the object's area turns the cursor
into a hand, and a click takes the object. Without Ctrl a click in the words
always places the caret. Tab and Select Next Object still reach it.
3 Four modes, not Word's seven
Not asked yet. Recommended: four now; tight and through need a contour and 'in
line' makes the object a character, so imported ones keep their original and 'in
line' comes later as an anchor kind of its own.
4 One key, cycling (D1064)
Decided: one entry, Wrap Text, Ctrl+Alt+L, each press goes to the next mode.
Free in all three manifests; no digit keys, which German AltGr uses. Where the
distance is set is open.
5 Where the wrap is kept
Not asked yet. Recommended: in the anchor next to dx and dy (D1023), with a
method set_wrap so that the history says 'Wrap text around Picture 1'.
6 Default for a new object (D1061)
Decided: Above and below. Proposed, not yet confirmed: switch it on when the
editor draws the wrap, so what is seen is what prints; until then print and
preview wrap and the editor does not.
